root_cause: All Windows post-commit dependency-install steps use PIP_INDEX_URL pointed at the in-cluster pip proxy (pip-proxy.pip-proxy.svc.cluster.local), which serves the PyPI JSON simple-index API. In this run the proxy returned a truncated or malformed JSON body (parsing fails deterministically at the same byte offset, char 33790, across every affected job and every Python version), so pip's json.loads() raises JSONDecodeError while resolving unrelated packages (torchvision, python API test deps, TF/JAX/PyTorch model requirements, ml-dtypes/keras). The identical column offset across independently-running jobs strongly indicates the proxy is serving a cached/broken response (e.g., a corrupted cache entry or a response truncated by a proxy-side size/timeout limit) rather than a per-job or per-package problem; no product source code is implicated.
reproduction_steps: N/A (depends on the internal pip-proxy's cached/served response at a specific point in time; not reproducible from a local clone). To probe: curl -s http://pip-proxy.pip-proxy.svc.cluster.local/simple/torch/ (or torchvision/tensorflow/etc.) from a runner with access to the proxy and check whether the JSON response is valid/complete with `python3 -c "import json,sys; json.load(sys.stdin)"`.
recommended_actions: Escalate to the CI infrastructure/runner team owning pip-proxy.pip-proxy.svc.cluster.local to inspect proxy logs/cache around 2026-09-30T02:41-02:58Z for truncated responses or upstream PyPI JSON API errors.
Add proxy-side response validation (or a cache-busting retry) so pip-proxy never forwards a truncated JSON body to clients.

Consider adding automatic pip retry-on-JSONDecodeError logic (e.g., `pip install --retries` plus a short backoff, or falling back to the public PyPI index) in the Windows dependency-install steps to reduce sensitivity to transient proxy glitches.
Monitor whether this recurs at the same byte offset (char 33790); a stable offset across many packages suggests a fixed-size buffer/truncation bug in the proxy rather than package-specific content.
prevention_strategies: Add health checks / synthetic pip-proxy JSON validation on a schedule so a corrupted proxy cache is detected before it causes a wave of post-commit failures across many jobs. Consider a fallback PIP_INDEX_URL or automatic retry with a fresh connection when pip raises JSONDecodeError while talking to the internal proxy.
historical_context: No prior post-commit investigation with this exact signature exists in the pattern database as of this run (first occurrence of the pip-proxy malformed-JSON signature).
